title: a `neural_block` integer field at exactly 2**32 is rejected — the descriptor's fields are capped at uint32
error_substring: param_width must be a non-negative integer
why: The runtime layer has always capped its own derived buffer sizes at
2**32, but the descriptor's own integer fields (in_degree, out_degree,
and the width fields) previously had no upper bound, only a lower one.
This fixture closes that gap: each of the six neural integer fields is
now capped at strictly less than 2**32, checked alongside the existing
The value used is exactly 4294967296 (2**32), not one less, so this pins
that the cap fires at the boundary itself, not merely somewhere above it.
`param_width` is the field used here (rather than `in_degree`, which a
different fixture already exercises for a non-numeric value), so this
also confirms the cap applies to the one field whose lower bound allows
zero, not just the fields that must be strictly positive.
Both languages parse this value as an ordinary large integer without any
special handling, so the cap is exercised directly rather than through
The fixture is otherwise identical to row01's golden with only this field
changed, so the only thing that can make it reject is the cap under test.
The manifest-bypassing plugin loader is exercised too, since its only
structural gate is the shared validator.
